All three fixed, tested against your real AIArchives repo, and installed.

**TPS arrow.** It was comparing 10s windows — early in any turn the previous window was always empty, so the arrow froze on ↑. Now the rate is a 3-second average and the trend compares the last 3s against the 3s before it. Verified live: ↑287 → ↓91 → ↑224 across one generation.

**Bottom lock — properly this time.** The previous fix only kept the input mounted; the region still floated up under the transcript. Now the dynamic area spans the full terminal height with a spacer in the middle, so the input bar and the status text under it are physically pinned to the last rows of the screen — fresh session, mid-stream, idle, always. The transcript shows its most recent tail directly above the input (an oversized answer shows `✦ …` plus its last lines, with the complete copy already flushed to your terminal's scrollback), and older items flow up into scrollback as new ones arrive. Stream capping is now wrap-aware and the region hard-clips, which also killed the line-corruption artifacts I caught mid-stream during testing.

**The max-effort fabrication in your trace.** That "illustrative package.json with mocha/cors" answer was pure invention. Three things now attack it: the prompt explicitly bans "typical contents / likely / illustrative / presumably" descriptions of unread files and requires reading every file mentioned; a new assumption-check guard bounces final answers containing those guess-markers back with orders to read the real files; and I re-ran your exact question on `/home/lane/AIArchives` at max effort — it now does `ls` + `read_file package.json` first and reports the real dependencies (Express + http-proxy-middleware, the actual `start`/`start:host` scripts) instead of the invented mocha/chai project, ending with an offer to read deeper rather than fabricating the rest.
